fieldValues.title: An outline-scaffolding record's own content field being empty does not mean it is childless — check its outbound relations before deleting
fieldValues.summary: A prior finding (51845c8c, filed from #629) generalised "empty content field, homed only to keep the tree total" to "safe to delete" across four design-note records. It held for three of four. The fourth still carried a live child through an outbound contains edge the finding did not check for — a table record holding the real content, extracted out of the note by an earlier one-off migration script. Before deleting any record flagged as empty scaffolding, run srs relation list and check for BOTH directions: the inbound edge that homed it (expected) and any outbound edge (a sign it still contains real content one hop down).
fieldValues.rationale:
Found working srs#636 (delete the four empty outline design-notes named in #629, dispatched 2026-09-06 19:19Z). The issue itself anticipated the risk ("If any turns out to carry content, leave it and say so") but the earlier finding that recommended the deletion did not check outbound relations, only the content field. srs relation list --repo srs showed Design Decisions, Usage Guidance and Extension Design Notes each with exactly one relation — the inbound contains edge from their concept — and all three were verified content-empty and childless, then deleted. mu-Democracy Mapping had two relations: the same inbound edge, plus an outbound contains edge to a table record whose intro field held the live SCDS-to-muDemocracy vocabulary mapping. scripts/migrate-tables.mjs, a pre-programme one-off migration (PR #544), explained why: it split embedded markdown tables out of several design-notes into standalone table records and blanked the parent's content field as part of that extraction, which is exactly what makes an extraction target look identical to true scaffolding under a content-field-only check.

The cost of skipping this check would have been silently deleting a record that still contains live content, which is a stronger error than merely widening the issue's scope: a contains edge asserts semantic composition (R8, the relation-design-principles design note), and a record with an outbound contains edge is by definition not a leaf, regardless of its own content field.

What generalizes: any finding or unit that judges a record's deletability from one field never checked the shape the concept-tree itself uses to mean "has children" — the outbound contains edge. A content-only check will pass on any record whose payload moved to a child rather than being deleted outright, which the migrate-tables-style split does routinely. Re-derive "childless" from srs relation list, not from re-reading a prior finding's claim.
